mechanism_narrative: A positive 3-month change in housing starts (HOUST) relative to the prior 3-month period (HOUST_t-2mo - HOUST_t-5mo > 0) indicates strengthening residential demand, which is associated with positive S&P 500 forward 20-day returns due to improved consumer spending and business investment.
failure_condition: The 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 60% of instances where the 3-month change in HOUST is positive.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) exceeds 4.0%, it signals a restrictive monetary policy that increases discount rates for equity valuation, leading to negative S&P 500 forward 20-day returns.
failure_condition: The 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of instances when FEDFUNDS > 4.0.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous increase in private employment (PAYEMS) and consumer spending (RSAFS) over the prior 3 months (PAYEMS_t-2mo > PAYEMS_t-5mo and RSAFS_t-2mo > RSAFS_t-5mo) indicates robust economic expansion, which is associated with positive S&P 500 forward 20-day returns.
failure_condition: The 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 60% of instances where both PAYEMS and RSAFS increased over the prior 3 months.

mechanism_narrative: In late-cycle economic expansions (defined by UNRATE < 5.0 and GDP growth > 2.0% annualized), a federal funds rate above 3.5% signals monetary tightening that increases equity discount rates, producing negative S&P 500 forward 20-day returns.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE < 5.0 AND GDPC1 growth > 2.0% AND FEDFUNDS > 3.5
failure_condition: The 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of instances where UNRATE < 5.0, GDPC1 growth > 2.0%, and FEDFUNDS > 3.5.

mechanism_narrative: A decline in industrial production (INDPRO) below 115.0 indicates weakening manufacturing activity, which is associated with negative S&P 500 forward 20-day returns due to reduced corporate output and earnings.
failure_condition: The 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of instances when INDPRO < 115.0.

mechanism_narrative: A positive 3-month change in industrial production (INDPRO) relative to the prior 3-month period (INDPRO_t-2mo - INDPRO_t-5mo > 0) indicates strengthening manufacturing activity, which is associated with positive S&P 500 forward 20-day returns.
failure_condition: The 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 60% of instances where INDPRO increased over the prior 3 months.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the consumer price index (CPIAUCSL) over the prior 3 months (CPIAUCSL_t-2mo - CPIAUCSL_t-5mo > 0.5) indicates accelerating inflation, which is associated with negative S&P 500 forward 5-day returns due to immediate monetary policy concerns.
failure_condition: The 5-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of instances when CPIAUCSL increased by more than 0.5 over the prior 3 months.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) below 5.0% over the prior 6 months (UNRATE_t-2mo < 5.0) indicates a tight labor market, which is associated with positive S&P 500 forward 60-day returns due to robust consumer spending and corporate earnings growth.
failure_condition: The 60-day forward returns are negative in more than 60% of instances when UNRATE < 5.0.
